transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-02-08 15:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jamal (Redwood SE), Priya, Tomás, Sara (LakeMist)

Summary: quick console walkthrough focused on per-route usage, cost-slice breakdowns, and routing/fallback policies for LakeMist's mixed latency and batch workloads. Customer wants pilot with two endpoints first and security docs.

Topics: Console overview, per-route dashboards, costing attribution, caching and KV cash (transcription), dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, pilot scope and timeline, SOC2/KMS questions.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, account exec on the Redwood side, joining with Jamal who is our solution eng. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya: good, thanks. we have about an hour — hoping to get a clear sense of how you show per-route costs and how we'd run a pilot without exposing raw data.
[00:15] Tomás: and also, we'll need to know how billing maps back to our internal routes for chargeback.
[00:20] Jamal: great, that's what we'll focus on. i'll start with a 10 minute tour of the console — usage lens, then per-route dashboards and the cost slice view, and then we'll dive into caching and routing policies.
[00:30] Sarah(?): /Sara: sounds good.
[00:33] Jamal: okay loading the console — you'll see here the main usage timeline, tokens in and tokens out, latency p50/p95. one thing you'll notice is the route legend on the left — we group based on your route tags which can be whatever you set at ingestion.
[00:48] Priya: quick question: will those tags map to our service names in k8s? or do we need a custom mapping?
[00:53] Jamal: you can push tags through the SDK or the routing layer, yep — we also have auto-infers for common fields. in practice most customers send a route header that maps directly to service id.
[01:07] Tomás: is there a sample integration doc?
[01:10] Maya: i'll drop the integration snippet and the route mapping guide in the notes after.
[01:15] [01:16] Jamal: switching to per-route panel — here we can pick a route and see the token breakdown, model variant used, batch sizes, and the cost per 1k tokens. the cost slice view breaks compute vs model vs infra overhead.
[01:29] Priya: can we split out streaming calls vs batch? we have both — streaming for interactive, batch for async reconciliation.
[01:35] Jamal: yes, we surface call type. streaming shows latency histograms; batch shows throughput and batching efficiency. one note on the math — batching improves cost per token but can add variability to p95 latency, so you'll see a toggle to model cost optimized or latency optimized.
[01:52] Priya: hmmm, on that, our SLO is pretty strict for chat feature — p95 under 600ms. excessive batching would be a hard no.
[01:58] Jamal: understood, you can pin that route to a latency-first policy. we'll also show where autoscaling breached and fallback to cheaper model variants when capacity hits limits.
[02:10] Tomás: when you say fallback, does that happen automatically? and can we control it per route?
[02:15] Jamal: yes it's policy driven — route level controls. you can say allow fallback to quantized variants or to lower-cost instance pool. we include a graded cooldown and alerting so ops isn't surprised.
[02:29] Sara: would that affect response shape? we have structured outputs.
[02:33] Jamal: only if you allow certain variants that don't support function calling or structured outputs. you'll see an incompatibility flag in the rollout UI.
[02:42] [02:45] Priya: security — we need to keep payloads in our VPC and not have logs shipped. can you run private?
[02:50] Maya: for pilot we can do Redwood Hosted with private tenancy (dedicated) or Private VPC. Jamal can explain tradeoffs.
[02:57] Jamal: Private gives you customer-managed network, KMS integration, and audit logs. Dedicated hosted gives isolation and easier onboarding. both options support no-logging mode and token redaction.
[03:12] Tomás: how does key rotation work with your KMS?
[03:15] Jamal: we integrate with major KMS providers — rotation policies are customer side, and Redwood supports envelope encryption. we can include a short SOC2 excerpt which describes key handling.
[03:25] Priya: perfect, that's critical.
[03:27] Jamal: back to the console — drill into a route and we show top prompt templates, sample latency per prompt length, long tail tokens. you can upload your prompt set as an eval to monitor quality drift.
[03:39] Priya: can the console alert on quality regressions tied to a prompt set?
[03:42] Jamal: yes, Redwood Optimize ties prompt-based evals to regression alerts. we'll show a baseline diff if a model update changes outputs.
[03:51] [04:00] Maya: quick qualification: what's the timeline for pilot?
[04:03] Priya: we want a two-week pilot in prod-ish traffic by mid march — goal is to validate cost per route and ops automation.
[04:10] Maya: ok so March 15th target. is there any procurement constraints?
[04:14] Sara: we require SOC2, SAML SSO, and a data processing addendum.
[04:20] Maya: we'll provide all those docs.
[04:22] Tomás: also curious about attribution — how granular is the billing export? we want per-route daily CSV to feed our internal chargeback system.
[04:30] Jamal: export supports per-route, per-model, per-instance metrics. you can pull daily CSVs via API or S3 push. it also includes token counts and cost columns so your FinOps can reconcile.
[04:42] Priya: do you have visibility into KV cache hits? we use KV to reduce recompute.
[04:47] Jamal: yes, cache hit ratios are in the route panel — although sometimes the transcriber here writes KV cash — but it's cache hit ratio. higher hits reduce token delta and show as reduced compute cost in the slice.
[04:58] [05:00] Sara: any limit on retention of traces? we have strict retention policies.
[05:03] Jamal: retention is configurable by plan; for Private you can set custom retention and self-host log retention. Hosted default is 90 days but Enterprise can extend.
[05:12] Priya: when you do automated batching, how do you measure the cost tradeoff?
[05:18] Jamal: the console simulates per-route projected cost under different batching thresholds — you can run a what-if with e.g., max batch size 16 vs 64 and see predicted unit cost and latency delta.
[05:30] Tomás: can we hook our internal anomaly detection to the console alerts?
[05:34] Jamal: yes we have webhook alerts and a prometheus exporter for metrics. many customers pipe events into their existing alerting stacks.
[05:42] [05:46] Priya: curious about multi-region routing — we have EU and NA users, want data residency rules.
[05:50] Jamal: routing policies support region pinning and fallback; you can set a rule to keep EU routes in eu-central and only fall back to a different region under emergency with explicit audit reason.
[06:02] Sara: and cost implications? cross-region failover would incur egress and possibly different instance pricing, correct?
[06:08] Jamal: yes the cost slice will show region premium and egress; the route page surfaces expected unit cost per region.
[06:15] [06:20] Maya: jumping ahead — pilot success criteria?
[06:22] Priya: 1) accurate per-route cost mapping to our internal chargeback 2) p95 <600ms for chat route 3) security docs cleared 4) no PII in logs.
[06:33] Maya: good. we should capture that in the next steps.
[06:36] Jamal: demo time — i'm going to simulate a high-traffic window and show the cost slice shifting as batches fill and as we hit autoscale.
[06:44] [06:48] Jamal: hmmm loading sample dataset — ok here you see spike at 11:34, autoscaler brought up two extra pools, and fallback attempted a quantized variant for non-chat routes. you can see cost per token for the chat route remained stable because it was pinned to latency-first.
[07:07] Priya: nice, can you export that snapshot and send it?
[07:10] Jamal: yep i'll export and attach to the follow-up.
[07:14] Tomás: on quantized variant — what's the expected drop in quality we should expect?
[07:18] Jamal: depends on model family. typical decimal loss in nlg metrics, but we tie evals to prompts to practically measure quality impact. sometimes it's negligible for canned completion tasks, worse for instruction-following.
[07:31] [07:40] Priya: one operational concern — our legal requires an IP flow diagram for any third party that sees model outputs. do you have a template?
[07:46] Maya: yes we have an architecture diagram pack. i'll send it with the SOC2 excerpt.
[07:51] Jamal: also note our private deployment diagram differs slightly if you go with VPC egress block.
[07:58] [08:05] Priya: pricing question — how granular are committed discounts for dedicated pools? we have variable qps across month.
[08:11] Maya: we offer reserved capacity with burst credits; pricing is tiered by committed GPU hours with a smoothing allowance. for variable workloads customers often do a small commit plus burst to cover spikes.
[08:24] Tomás: would that show up in the console? ability to see committed vs burst consumption?
[08:28] Jamal: yes consumption meter is in billing tab; you can also export a forecast.
[08:33] [08:40] Priya: what's the onboarding timeline realistically?
[08:42] Maya: for a pilot it's typically 2-3 weeks (policy + console setup + sandbox), production rollout usually 6-8 weeks if Private is chosen.
[08:52] Sara: procurement question — do you accept PO?
[08:55] Maya: yes enterprise accepts PO with agreed terms. we'll have legal and procurement contacts after this.
[09:00] [09:10] Jamal: ok last quick walk — the cost attribution flow: console ingests route metadata, correlates tokens -> model footprint -> instance hours, applies discounts, and produces per-route cost and exportable CSVs. there's also a reconciliation engine to match invoices.
[09:26] Priya: can we map costs down to feature flag or product bucket, not just route?
[09:31] Jamal: yes if you emit a feature tag we can slice by that dimension; many customers use feature tags for product chargeback.
[09:38] [09:45] Maya: i want to recap next steps now.
[09:47] Priya: please.
[09:48] Maya: 1) we'll send SOC2 excerpt, SAML SSO guide, and integration snippets (Maya). 2) Jamal will stand up a sandbox that mirrors your route tags and push anonymized telemetry for the demo (Jamal). 3) Tomás to provide two example endpoints and traffic pattern for pilot (Tomás). 4) set pilot target start March 15th and we'll confirm timeline by Feb 15th.
[10:12] Tomás: sounds good.
[10:15] Priya: any blockers on Redwood side?
[10:18] Maya: none. we'll also include cost examples for committed vs burst pricing.
[10:23] [10:30] Sara: thanks everyone.
[10:32] Jamal: thanks, we'll follow up with the attachments.
[10:35] Maya: thanks all. meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript mangled some technical terms (KV cache -> KV cash; quantized -> quantizeed at moments). speaker labels occasionally generic.

References shared: integration-snippet.md (link in follow-up), SOC2-excerpt.pdf, pilot-pricing-sheet.xlsx, sample-export-snapshot-2027-02-08.csv
